name: The Last Architect
desc: From the silent heart of a dead star, a signal answers the galaxy's scream. The Last Architect is the final, lingering thought of a race that built universes, a benevolent cosmic force awakened by the escalating chaos of the Interregnum. It is not a creature, but a manifestation of pure, ordered energy. It appears as a vast, intricate, and beautiful mandala of crystalline golden light and impossible, self-assembling geometry. Its light is warm and serene, a stark contrast to the cold darkness of the Silent King. It is a force of pure creation against the encroaching void. Its presence on the battlefield is restorative. It cannot be attacked, but its passive energy rebuilds destroyed units, heals the wounded, and erects powerful defensive pylons. It is the universe's immune system, a dormant power of order and hope awakening to mend what was broken.

name: The Silent King
desc: The Silent King is not a creature, a machine, or a god. It is an echo. It is a sliver of the Outer God's consciousness, a temporary avatar given form in our dimension. It is a figure of pure cosmic horror, appearing as a massive, humanoid silhouette made of pure darkness, within which a galaxy of stars slowly turns. It is crowned with a halo of fractured, floating Architect geometry. It does not speak, for its thoughts are creation and destruction. It does not move, for it is already everywhere. Its presence on the battlefield is a fundamental violation of reality. It cannot be attacked, for it is not truly there. Instead, the universe itself begins to unravel around it. Enemy units slowly erode, their matter decaying into nothingness. If it remains on the battlefield long enough, reality collapses entirely. It is the ultimate expression of the Cult's faith: the end of our reality, and the beginning of their god's.

name: Grand Admiral Eva Rostova
desc: Grand Admiral Eva Rostova is the supreme commander of the Terran Mandate's fleet and, arguably, the single most important individual holding the remnants of human civilization together. She is an older, dignified woman, a strategic genius who rose from the rank of Gunnery Sergeant to command the entire navy. She is always depicted on the command bridge of her flagship, the TFS Endeavour, surrounded by holographic displays. She is not a frontline warrior, but her mind is the Mandate's greatest weapon. Her flawless strategies and unwavering resolve have saved the Mandate from collapse a dozen times over. Her presence in a system provides massive strategic bonuses, her commands unlocking the full potential of the fleet. She is the living embodiment of the Mandate's enduring spirit, the last great leader from an age of heroes.

name: Board of Directors
desc: The Aurigan Trade Syndicate is not ruled by a person; it is ruled by a principle. The Board of Directors is the ultimate expression of this. It is not a council of individuals, but a shadowy, abstract entity representing the cold, inhuman logic of pure capitalism. On the battlefield, its "presence" is not physical, but a manifestation of its total control over the galactic markets and information networks. When the Board focuses its attention on a conflict, the Syndicate's forces become terrifyingly efficient. Resources flow in at an accelerated rate, advanced prototypes are deployed from corporate black sites, and enemy systems are crippled by economic warfare. The Board is the ultimate power of the Syndicate, a faceless, profit-driven god that can buy and sell entire star systems with a single, silent directive.

name: The Silent Voice
desc: The Chorus is a hive mind, but every symphony needs a conductor. The Silent Voice is the psychic nexus of the swarm, a primary synapse creature that coordinates the actions of billions of Chorus organisms across entire sectors of space. It is not a commander in the traditional sense; it does not think, it is. It is a being of pure, malevolent consciousness, a grotesque fusion of brain matter, Aetherium crystals, and alien technology, usually found at the heart of the largest Chorus infestations. Its psychic presence on the battlefield is a crushing weight on the minds of its enemies, while its silent commands coordinate the swarm with perfect, terrifying efficiency. To defeat the Silent Voice is to temporarily deafen the Chorus, to throw the swarm into chaos. But it is only a temporary victory, for the Chorus is vast, and there are always other voices waiting in the silence.

name: Aegis-Class Heavy Cruiser
desc: The Aegis-Class Heavy Cruiser is one of the few true warships left in the Terran Mandate's arsenal. Unlike the smaller, retrofitted Frigates, the Aegis was built for one purpose: to bring overwhelming naval power to bear against the enemies of the Federation. It is a massive, powerful vessel, bristling with weapon emplacements, its spine dominated by a colossal Magnetic Accelerator Cannon. These ships are rare and precious, each one a symbol of the Mandate's dwindling but still potent industrial might. They are the centerpiece of any major Mandate fleet, capable of going toe-to-toe with the largest vessels the other factions can field. To lose an Aegis is a catastrophic blow to the Mandate, but to deploy one is to signal that the time for defense is over, and the time for retribution has begun.

name: Orbital Defense Platform
desc: In the golden age, the Federation ringed its core worlds with these silent, colossal guardians. An Orbital Defense Platform is a massive, stationary space station, a fortress armed with ship-to-ship cannons powerful enough to threaten a heavy cruiser. Most were decommissioned or fell into disrepair during the collapse, but the Mandate has reactivated the few that remain. They are a purely defensive asset, an immovable shield for the Mandate's most vital worlds. Their presence in a system can halt an entire invasion fleet, their overwhelming firepower forcing an enemy to either commit to a costly frontal assault or abandon their attack entirely. They are a symbol of the Federation's forgotten might, a testament to a time when humanity built things meant to last forever.

name: Brood-Ship
desc: The Brood-Ship is a cosmic horror of unimaginable scale. It was once a civilian colony vessel, a city-sized starship that was home to half a million souls. Now, it is a womb. The Chorus has completely assimilated it, its original structure almost entirely obscured by pulsating organic growths, chitinous armor, and vast, fleshy sacs. It moves not with engines, but by undulating through the void like a vast cosmic leviathan. It is a living, breeding hive that travels between the stars. Its purpose is not to fight, but to overwhelm. In battle, it hangs in orbit, its only function to constantly spawn new Chorus units onto the battlefield, a relentless tide of biological horrors that can drown even the most fortified planet in a sea of flesh and claws. It does not travel to a destination; it brings the destination with it.

name: Spartan-001 'The Vindicator'
desc: In the final, desperate days of the Federation, a program was initiated to create the ultimate soldier, a warrior to hold back the encroaching darkness. The program was a success, but it was too little, too late. Spartan-001, known only as 'The Vindicator', is the last survivor of that program. He is a living legend, a relic from a more heroic age. He is a towering figure in a unique suit of master-crafted power armor inspired by the knights of Old Earth, a bridge between the Federation's golden age and the Mandate's grim present. He is a one-man army, a strategic asset capable of turning the tide of any battle. He fights with a quiet, sorrowful fury, not for the Mandate as it is, but for the Federation it was meant to be. He is the ghost of a fallen Camelot, his sword the last bastion of a forgotten ideal.

name: High Diviner Kaelen Marr
desc: Kaelen Marr is the High Diviner, the prophet of the Outer God. He is a legendary figure who has achieved a level of symbiosis with Aetherium that borders on transcendence. He is an ancient, wizened figure, his eyes glowing with the pure blue energy of the Spice of Dune, constantly surrounded by a swirling cloud of Aetherium dust. To him, the future is not a mystery; it is a landscape. He sees all possible timelines, the infinite threads of fate shimmering around him. He does not see the battles of the Interregnum as a war, but as a minor, predictable spasm in a vast, cosmic play. His power is not in direct combat, but in controlling fate itself. He can guide his followers along the one timeline that leads to victory, ensuring they have the right miracle at the right moment, and that their enemies' best-laid plans will always, inevitably, fail.

name: Frigate 'Duty's Resolve'
desc: The 'Duty's Resolve' is more than just a starship; it is a living piece of history. This Constitution-class vessel was launched in the golden age of the Federation, a vessel of peace and exploration. Now, her elegant, curved hull is scarred by a hundred battles, patched with crude, angular armor plates. Her science labs are filled with munitions, and her observation decks are lined with point-defense cannons. She is old, she is tired, but her resolve, like that of her crew, is unbroken. As a Frigate, she is not the most powerful ship in the Mandate's fleet, but she is a versatile and crucial asset. She can provide powerful orbital fire support, deploy squads of Marines to key locations, and engage smaller enemy vessels. She is a symbol of the Mandate itself: a beautiful relic of a better time, reluctantly but effectively turned into a weapon of war.

name: Scorpion MBT
desc: The M808 "Scorpion" Main Battle Tank is the iron fist of the Terran Mandate. In an era where many factions favor speed or esoteric powers, the Scorpion is a monument to the simple, brutal effectiveness of heavy armor and overwhelming firepower. This slow, heavily armored behemoth is the centerpiece of any major Mandate ground assault. Its powerful main cannon can obliterate enemy vehicles and fortifications, while its multiple machine guns provide anti-infantry support. To face a line of Scorpions advancing across an open field is a daunting prospect for any commander. It is a symbol of the Mandate's more traditional, ground-based military doctrine, a rolling fortress that can take incredible punishment and deliver even more in return.

name: Cathedral Tank "Wrath's Hymn"
desc: The "Wrath's Hymn" is a blasphemous and terrifying fusion of a holy shrine and a weapon of mass destruction. This massive, slow-moving war machine resembles a mobile gothic cathedral, complete with stained-glass viewports, ornate buttresses, and towering spires that are actually sophisticated sensor arrays. Its primary armament is a set of immense "Organ Pipe" missile launchers that can fire a devastating, long-range barrage. As it advances, it broadcasts the Cult's terrifying hymns across the battlefield, a psychological weapon as potent as its physical one. It is a rolling testament to the Cult's core belief: that faith is the greatest weapon, and that there is no corner of life, not even the tools of war, that should not be consecrated to the glory of the Outer God.

name: Nanite Swarm
desc: The Nanite Swarm is one of the Syndicate's most illegal and terrifying weapons, a direct violation of Federation-era prohibitions on self-replicating technology. It is a "grey goo" weapon, a shimmering, roiling cloud of microscopic machines unleashed on the battlefield. The swarm is programmed with a single, simple directive: disassemble all matter—organic or mechanical—in a designated area. It is a weapon of absolute area denial. Infantry caught in the cloud are stripped to their component atoms in seconds. Vehicles and structures are slowly but inexorably consumed, their materials used by the swarm to replicate and grow. It is an indiscriminate, uncontrollable horror, a weapon the Syndicate only deploys when it has decided that a particular asset is no longer worth acquiring, and must simply be erased from existence.

name: Rogue Architect Sentinel
desc: The Architects did not vanish without leaving guardians behind. A Rogue Architect Sentinel is a dormant defense drone, a crystalline entity of impossible geometry, left to protect a key site. Awakened by the chaos of the Interregnum, its ancient programming has become corrupted. It no longer recognizes friend from foe; it sees all lesser life as a threat to be neutralized. It moves with an eerie, silent grace, its form shimmering and phasing in and out of reality. It attacks any and all factions that approach its territory with devastatingly powerful energy weapons that can slice through the heaviest armor. It is a dangerous and unpredictable relic of a lost age, a reminder that the Architects' power, even when broken and malfunctioning, is still far beyond human comprehension.

name: Archon
desc: An Archon is a high-ranking priest of the Cult whose connection to the Outer God has granted them terrifying psychic power. They levitate slightly off the ground, their faces hidden behind ornate, impassive golden masks, surrounded by a faint aura of Aetherium energy. They do not need to carry weapons, for their mind is their weapon. An Archon can reach into the thoughts of an enemy commander, stealing their battle plans. They can project illusions, force an enemy to discard their strategies, or even temporarily seize control of a lesser-willed soldier, turning them against their comrades. They are the manipulators of the battlefield, their power a subtle but devastating force that can unravel an opponent's entire strategy without firing a single shot. They are a testament to the maddening truth the Cult embraces: reality is a thin veil, and they have learned how to pull at its threads.

name: Revenant Cyber-Ninja
desc: The "Revenant" is the pinnacle of the Syndicate's cybernetic assassination programs. While the Infiltrator is a ghost, the Revenant is a phantom. These elite operatives have had their bodies almost entirely replaced with top-of-the-line, military-grade cybernetics, granting them superhuman speed, strength, and reflexes. Their purpose is singular: to hunt and eliminate enemy hero characters. They move in a blur of motion, their glowing energy katanas capable of parrying heavy weapons and slicing through power armor. They are the Syndicate's answer to the Mandate's Helljumper Captains and the Cult's powerful Archons. They are exceedingly expensive to produce and maintain, but for the Syndicate, the guaranteed removal of a key enemy leader is always a profitable investment.

name: Siege Mech
desc: The 'Arbitrator' Class Siege Mech is not a weapon of war; it is an instrument of hostile asset acquisition. This colossal, bipedal war machine towers over the battlefield, its design brutally angular and industrial, reflecting the cold, corporate efficiency of the Syndicate. It is deployed when a planetary board of directors fails to see the value of a merger. Armed with massive, multi-barreled cannons, shoulder-mounted missile pods, and a huge industrial claw for dismantling fortifications, it is incredibly slow but possesses overwhelming firepower and durability. Its purpose is not to fight armies, but to systematically dismantle cities and fortresses, to break the will of any who would resist the Syndicate's advance. It is a very persuasive tool.

name: Helljumper Captain
desc: We jump feet first into hell. This is the motto of the Orbital Drop Shock Troopers, the elite of the Mandate Marine Corps, and the Helljumper Captain is the best of the best. These are the charismatic, battle-hardened leaders who lead the most dangerous missions. Clad in advanced, darker-colored armor and a distinctive, sleek helmet, the Captain is a symbol of courage and competence. They are the first to drop from orbit and the last to be extracted. Their presence on the battlefield is a massive boon to morale; a Helljumper Captain's command inspires all friendly Mandate units to fight harder, aim truer, and hold the line longer. They are a living embodiment of the Mandate's highest ideals, a hero in an age that has precious few of them.

name: Tarantula Mining Walker
desc: The Syndicate wastes nothing. The "Tarantula" was originally a six-legged industrial machine, a walker designed for strip-mining operations in hazardous environments. When war broke out, the Syndicate's engineers saw no need to design a new heavy walker from scratch. They simply repurposed the Tarantula. Its powerful, precision mining lasers proved just as effective at slicing through vehicle armor as they were at cutting through rock, and its heavy manipulator claws, designed to lift tons of ore, could tear a tank apart with ease. It is a slow, cumbersome machine, but its heavy industrial armor makes it incredibly durable. It is a perfect example of the Syndicate's brutal pragmatism and its belief that the only difference between a tool and a weapon is its target.

name: Abomination
desc: The Abomination is a walking monument to the Chorus's ultimate goal: the end of all individuality. It is not a single creature; it is a committee, a horrifying fusion of multiple assimilated beings. This towering, asymmetrical brute might be composed of the fused bodies of a dozen soldiers, their commander, and the tank they were piloting, all screaming with a single, silent voice. A tank tread might serve as a leg, a cluster of human torsos forms its main body, and multiple arms—some organic, some mechanical—sprout from its form, each wielding a different corrupted weapon. It is a terrifying and durable frontline unit, designed to smash through enemy defenses and absorb huge amounts of damage. It is the ultimate expression of the Chorus's corrupting influence, a living collage of body horror that can break the morale of even the most hardened soldiers.

name: Bile Launcher
desc: The Bile Launcher is the Chorus's heavy artillery, a disgusting but brutally effective weapon. It is a living siege engine, a massive, pulsating sac of hyper-corrosive fluids and parasitic larvae mounted on a corrupted, slow-moving chassis. With a sickening convulsion, it hurls large, explosive sacs of this vile payload across the battlefield. Upon impact, the sacs burst, showering a wide area in acid that can melt infantry and armor alike. Worse, the parasitic larvae can burrow into the flesh of survivors, slowly turning them into new Chorus hosts. It is a weapon of area denial and psychological terror, capable of breaking up enemy formations and turning fortified positions into death traps.

name: Zealot Squad
desc: A Zealot is an Initiate whose faith has been forged into a weapon. Having proven their devotion, they are granted partial suits of ornate, gothic-style plate armor and "glaives of faith"—large polearms that crackle with contained Aetherium energy. They are the frontline warriors of the Cult, their purpose to engage the enemy in glorious melee combat. They fight with a fanatical courage that unnerves even veteran soldiers, chanting hymns to the Outer God as they charge into gunfire. Their true strength, however, lies in their collective faith. A Zealot draws power from the martyrdom of their brethren; for each friendly unit that falls in battle, their resolve hardens and their strikes become more powerful. They are designed to thrive in the bloodiest, most desperate battles, turning the Cult's losses into a source of righteous, unstoppable fury.

name: Marksman Team
desc: Not all battles are won by overwhelming force. The Mandate, with its limited resources, understands the value of precision. A Marksman Team is a two-person unit, a sniper and a spotter, who represent the scalpel to the Marine Corps' hammer. Clad in ghillie-style cloaks over their armor, they are masters of stealth and patience. They can remain hidden for days, waiting for the perfect moment to strike. Their high-caliber anti-materiel rifle can punch through the armor of a Syndicate Enforcer or eliminate a Cult Archon from a mile away, sowing chaos and decapitating the enemy's command structure. They are a testament to the Mandate's professionalism, a quiet, lethal force that can change the course of a battle with a single, perfectly placed shot.

name: Viper Gunship
desc: The "Viper" Gunship embodies the Syndicate's combat philosophy: speed, precision, and overwhelming force applied to a single, profitable target. It is a sleek, fast-attack craft, its angular, insectoid design a hallmark of the Syndicate's non-human-centric aesthetic. It is not designed for prolonged dogfights or atmospheric patrols. Its purpose is to scream in from a low altitude, unleash a devastating barrage of missiles and cannon fire on a pre-designated high-value target—be it an enemy command center, a heavy tank, or a key piece of infrastructure—and then vanish before the enemy can mount an effective response. It is a surgical strike weapon, a tool for maximizing damage to enemy assets while minimizing risk to the Syndicate's own.

name: Assimilation Tendril
desc: The Assimilation Tendril is the slow, creeping horror of the Chorus made manifest. It is not a single creature, but a creeping, pulsating mass of Chorus biomass that advances across the battlefield like a living carpet of flesh. It is not fast, nor is it a direct threat to infantry. Its true purpose is far more insidious. When it encounters a damaged enemy vehicle or a weakened structure, it ensnares it, its tendrils forcing their way into every crack and seam. It slowly, methodically corrupts the machine's systems, fuses with its structure, and converts it into a new, loyal war machine for the hive mind. To see a Tendril slowly consuming a Mandate tank, its metal groaning as it is warped into a new, horrifying shape, is to understand the true, inexorable nature of the Chorus's victory.

name: Spitter Beast
desc: The "Spitter" Beast is a prime example of the Chorus's grotesque ingenuity. This creature was once a quadrupedal utility drone, perhaps a cargo hauler or a repair unit. The hive mind has repurposed it, its metallic chassis now barely visible beneath tumorous flesh and chitinous plates. A massive, translucent sac of hyper-corrosive acid churns on its back, and its head has been replaced with a bony, cannon-like orifice. It is a piece of mobile, living artillery. It cannot move and fire in the same turn, but its ranged attack is devastating, capable of melting infantry and corroding vehicle armor from a safe distance. It forces enemies to close in and deal with it directly, often drawing them into ambushes. It is a disgusting but highly effective battlefield unit, a symbol of the Chorus's ability to turn even the most mundane technology into a weapon of horror.

name: Gunnery Sergeant "Grizz"
desc: Gunnery Sergeant "Grizz" is a living legend within the Mandate Marine Corps, though he would be the first to deny it. He is a veteran of a hundred campaigns, his face a roadmap of scars and his armor a patchwork of field repairs and unauthorized modifications. He is the unbreakable backbone of whatever company he is assigned to, his booming voice and unwavering presence a source of inspiration for the younger Marines. He is not a strategic genius or a superhuman warrior; he is a master of the fundamentals of warfare, a grizzled professional who has survived through sheer grit and experience. His presence on the battlefield is a force multiplier, his tactical acumen and inspirational shouts turning a wavering line of Marines into an unbreakable wall of defiance. He is the embodiment of the Corps' spirit: stubborn, resilient, and too damn mean to die.

name: Penitent Engine
desc: For the Cult, heresy is a stain that can only be cleansed by death in the service of the Outer God. The Penitent Engine is this doctrine made manifest. A heretic who has spoken against the Cult's dogma is given a chance at absolution: they are surgically and irrevocably wired into the chassis of a bipedal war machine. Driven by constant pain and a flood of religious catechisms fed directly into their brain, the pilot becomes a berserker, a mindless instrument of the Cult's fury. Armed with massive flamethrowers to "purify" the unclean and industrial buzz-saws to tear apart enemy armor, the Penitent Engine charges headlong into the thickest fighting, its every action a desperate, agonizing prayer for forgiveness. It is a terrifying and tragic sight, a symbol of the Cult's absolute power and its cruel definition of redemption.

name: Broadsword Interceptor
desc: While the Mandate's ground forces often rely on older, retrofitted technology, their aerospace corps boasts some of the most advanced craft in the galaxy, a direct inheritance from the Federation's golden age. The "Broadsword" is the Mandate's primary space and atmospheric superiority fighter. It is a fast, agile, and deadly interceptor, designed for one purpose: hunting down and destroying enemy craft. Its sleek, aerodynamic design and powerful engines allow it to outmaneuver the Syndicate's gunships and the Cult's cumbersome converted shuttles. Armed with rapid-fire cannons and air-to-air missiles, a squadron of Broadswords can secure the skies, ensuring that ground forces are safe from orbital bombardment and that the Pelican dropships can deliver their precious cargo. It is a symbol of the Mandate's lingering technological edge.

name: Enforcer
desc: The Syndicate Enforcer is the cold, hard reality of corporate law. These elite soldiers are heavily augmented humans, their organic parts viewed as liabilities to be replaced with gleaming chrome and black polymer cybernetics. One arm is typically replaced with an integrated, multi-barreled firearm, while their eyes glow with the cold, blue light of targeting systems. They are deployed to collect on defaulted loans, break strikes, or eliminate competitors. They are more machine than human, their emotions suppressed by chemical regulators and their actions dictated by profit-loss calculations. On the battlefield, they are brutally efficient combatants, a significant step up from the expendable Shock Troopers, representing the Syndicate's willingness to invest heavily in assets that guarantee a return.

name: Infiltrator
desc: The most profitable hostile takeover is the one the target never sees coming. The Syndicate Infiltrator is a master of corporate espionage and assassination, a ghost in the machine. Clad in a sleek, black bodyglove that incorporates active camouflage technology, the Infiltrator can become nearly invisible, bypassing enemy lines and security systems with ease. They are androgynous, their identities completely concealed, representing the Syndicate's belief that individuality is a weakness. Armed with silenced pistols and monomolecular blades, their role is not to fight battles, but to end them before they begin by eliminating high-value targets, sabotaging key infrastructure, or stealing vital intelligence. They are the scalpel to the Siege Mech's hammer, a testament to the Syndicate's belief that a well-placed whisper can be more devastating than an artillery barrage.

name: Pelican Dropship
desc: The D77-TM, universally known as the "Pelican," is the workhorse of the Mandate Marine Corps. It is not sleek, it is not fast, and it is certainly not elegant. It is a flying armored box, a VTOL (Vertical Take-Off and Landing) troop transport designed for one purpose: getting soldiers into and out of the most dangerous places in the galaxy. Its hull is scarred and stained from countless combat drops, each dent a story of a mission survived. For a squad of Marines pinned down by enemy fire, the roar of a Pelican's engines is the sound of salvation. It can deliver troops for a flanking maneuver, extract wounded under fire, or deploy a Warthog for fire support. It is a symbol of hope and resilience, the embodiment of the Mandate's logistical strength and its unwavering commitment to its soldiers.

name: Relic Bearer
desc: Not all power in the Cult comes from sacrifice. Some comes from the preservation of holy artifacts. The Relic Bearer is an initiate given a singular, solemn duty: to carry a fragment of Architect technology into battle. These relics, often glowing with a faint internal light, are believed to be shards of the Outer God's physical form. The Bearer, protected by their faith and the relic's strange energy field, acts as a mobile shrine on the battlefield. The relic's aura can deflect bullets, soothe the minds of nearby cultists, and fill them with righteous fury. The Relic Bearer themselves are of little consequence; it is the artifact they carry that matters. They are a focal point for the Cult's power, a beacon of faith that inspires their brethren to fight and die with even greater fervor.

name: The Derelict
desc: It drifts in the void, a silent testament to a forgotten age of cosmic horror. The Derelict is a vast, crescent-shaped starship of unknown, non-human origin, its design a haunting fusion of skeletal, fossilized structures and advanced biomechanics. It is a direct and terrifying homage to the work of H.R. Giger. The ship crashed on a desolate moon thousands of years ago, but it is not truly dead. A faint, hypnotic signal still broadcasts from its shattered hull—not a call for help, but a lure. Those who dare to explore its silent, bone-lined corridors find that something still waits in the darkness. On the battlefield, its presence creates a zone of extreme hazard, as the ancient, predatory creatures that still inhabit its tomb periodically emerge to hunt, indifferent to faction allegiance.

name: Spore Chimney
desc: The Chorus does not need barracks or factories to create its armies. It simply grows them. A Spore Chimney is a stationary, organic tower of pulsating flesh and chitin, one of the first structures the Chorus erects after infesting a new world. It is a living factory, a grotesque monument to the swarm's reproductive efficiency. Periodically, the chimney convulses and spews a thick cloud of infectious spores into the atmosphere. Where these spores land, new, lesser Chorus creatures—like Skitterlings—are spawned, ready to serve the hive mind. A single Spore Chimney can quickly overwhelm a planetary defense force, its constant stream of reinforcements turning any battle into a war of attrition that only the Chorus can win. Destroying these structures is the top priority for any force hoping to halt the Chorus's inexorable advance.

name: Vision of Madness
desc: The Cult's most insidious weapons are not those that destroy the body, but those that shatter the mind. A Vision of Madness is a psychic shockwave, a focused blast of raw, chaotic energy unleashed by a gathering of the Cult's psykers. It is a weapon that cannot be stopped by armor or shields. Those caught in its path are assaulted with incomprehensible, terrifying truths from the Outer God's dimension. Their minds break, reality dissolves into a nightmare, and friend becomes foe. A disciplined squad of Mandate Marines might suddenly turn on each other, their rifles firing wildly, while a Syndicate Enforcer might simply stand frozen, screaming at horrors only it can see. It is a terrifying and unpredictable weapon, a perfect expression of the Cult's belief that the only true reality is the one their god wills.

name: Choir of the Void
desc: The Choir of the Void is the Cult's psychic artillery. This is a squad of acolytes whose minds have been opened to the whispers of the Outer God, but who lack the strength to become Archons or Diviners. Instead, their psychic potential is weaponized in a more direct, brutal fashion. Gathered on the battlefield, they begin a dissonant, chanting hymn, their voices combining into a psychic frequency that is deeply unsettling to the unconsecrated mind. This "hymn" does not cause direct harm, but it shatters enemy morale, erodes their will to fight, and fills them with a gnawing dread. Under the influence of the Choir, soldiers become hesitant, their aim falters, and their armor feels suddenly thin and useless. They are a potent psychological weapon, turning an enemy's own fear against them.

name: Warthog ATV
desc: The M12-M All-Terrain Vehicle, affectionately known as the "Warthog," is a relic of a simpler time. It has no energy shields, no anti-gravity plates, and no AI targeting systems. It is a machine of rugged simplicity: four heavy-duty tires, a powerful combustion engine, and a rear-mounted heavy machine gun. It has served the Mandate for centuries, a testament to the enduring quality of old Federation engineering. In an age of incomprehensible technology and cosmic horrors, the Warthog is a symbol of grounded, reliable functionality. It is used for reconnaissance, rapid fire support, and tactical repositioning, its iconic engine roar a familiar and welcome sound to any Marine in the field. It represents the Mandate's core philosophy: rely on what is proven, maintain what is valuable, and never forget the simple tools that helped build a better future.

name: Aetherium Anomaly
desc: Space-time is not a smooth, consistent fabric. In places, it is frayed and torn, wounded by the echoes of the Architects' impossible power. An Aetherium Anomaly is one such wound, a localized bubble of unstable reality. It is not a creature or a machine, but a shimmering, crystalline distortion in the air, crackling with multi-colored energy that bends light and defies physics. To approach one is to gamble with the fundamental laws of the universe. Units near an Anomaly might find their weapons supercharged, their armor hardened to impossible degrees, or they might find themselves aged to dust in an instant. These anomalies are a constant, unpredictable hazard on the battlefields of the Interregnum, a reminder that the greatest powers in the universe are indifferent to the petty squabbles of humanity.

name: Sacrificial Altar
desc: The Cult does not conquer territory; it consecrates it. A Sacrificial Altar is a structure of alien stone and warped metal, hastily erected on the battlefield and blessed by the Cult's priests. Carved with glowing, non-Euclidean glyphs, it acts as a focal point for the Outer God's attention. It is here that the Cult's philosophy of martyrdom is made manifest. Initiates and Zealots willingly offer their lives upon the altar, their life force channeled through the strange geometry to fuel the Cult's dark miracles. The air around an altar crackles with forbidden power, and with each sacrifice, the veil between realities grows thinner. For the Cult, it is a holy place, a direct line to their god. For their enemies, it is a symbol of the Cult's madness and a source of terrifying, unpredictable power.

name: Initiate
desc: To become an Initiate is to take the first step into the glorious, maddening truth of the Outer God. These are the newest converts to the Cult, their eyes opened to the "grand design" by the whispers of Aetherium. They cast aside their old lives, donning simple robes and porcelain masks to signify their rebirth. They are taught that their individual lives are meaningless, a single drop in the cosmic ocean of their god's consciousness. Their purpose is not to live, but to be spent. In battle, they march forward with a serenity that unnerves their enemies, carrying ceremonial daggers and blessed firearms. They know that their true value lies not in their skill at arms, but in the moment of their death. By sacrificing themselves, they fuel the Cult's dark miracles, their lives becoming the currency that pays for victory.

name: Corrupted Marine
desc: There are few sights more horrifying to a Mandate soldier than a Corrupted Marine. This creature was once a brother-in-arms, a disciplined professional dedicated to protecting humanity. Now, it is a puppet of the hive mind, its body and skills twisted to serve the swarm. Its Mandate armor is warped and shattered from within by grotesque biological growths, bone spikes piercing the ceramite plates. One arm has mutated into a fleshy cannon that spews corrosive bile, while the other still instinctively clutches a rifle it no longer understands. It retains its combat training, using cover and advancing with a terrifying parody of military tactics, but its loyalty is to the silent, all-consuming voice of the Chorus. It is a walking blasphemy, a symbol of the Chorus's ultimate victory: the turning of humanity's greatest defenders into its most terrifying monsters.

name: Auditor
desc: The Auditor is the Syndicate's presence on the battlefield, a physical manifestation of the Board of Directors' will. Clad in a sharp, sterile corporate suit and protected by a personal energy shield, the Auditor is a non-combatant who wields a power far greater than any rifle: the authority of the bottom line. They observe engagements from a safe distance, their datapads tracking asset performance, resource acquisition rates, and acceptable loss margins. Their presence ensures that every action taken is maximally profitable. They are despised by the mercenaries and shock troopers they oversee, as the Auditor's cold calculus often designates them as "acceptable losses." They are a chilling reminder that in the Syndicate's eyes, war is not a struggle for survival or ideology; it is a hostile takeover, and the Auditor is there to ensure it remains profitable.

name: Skitterling
desc: The first sign of a Chorus infestation is not a roar or a battle, but a faint, chittering sound in the vents. The Skitterling is the vanguard of the swarm, a small, fast, and horrifyingly efficient scout organism. Roughly the size of a large dog, this creature is a fusion of insectoid terror and Giger's biomechanics, all spindly legs and a segmented body with no discernible head—only a gaping maw and a pulsating neural sac. It moves with unnerving silence through the shadows of starships and colonies, a key that unlocks the door from the inside. Its purpose is not to fight armies, but to find the first weakness, the first isolated victim. Once it strikes, the process of assimilation begins, and the true horror of the Chorus is unleashed. By the time you see a Skitterling, the battle is already lost; you just don't know it yet.

name: Shock Trooper
desc: Where the Terran Mandate sees soldiers, the Aurigan Trade Syndicate sees assets. The Shock Trooper is the ultimate expression of this philosophy. Grown in nutrient vats and flash-trained through neural induction, these cloned soldiers are the Syndicate's answer to the problem of costly and unreliable human infantry. They are equipped with mass-produced armor and standard-issue pulse rifles, and they are utterly, chemically loyal to their corporate creators. They feel no fear, ask no questions, and their lives are a literal line item on a balance sheet. They are deployed in overwhelming numbers to secure corporate interests, their identical faces and unwavering obedience a chilling symbol of the Syndicate's belief that everything, even human life, can be manufactured, monetized, and ultimately, disposed of.

name: Field Medic
desc: Amidst the brutal pragmatism of the Interregnum, the Mandate Field Medic is a stubborn reminder of the Federation's most cherished ideal: the sanctity of every human life. Lightly armed and clad in armor marked with the ancient symbols of healing, the Medic's role is not to take lives, but to save them. They brave the heaviest fire, their bio-foam applicators and trauma kits their only weapons against the horrors of the modern battlefield. Each life they save is a small victory against the encroaching darkness, a defiance of the cynical calculus of the Syndicate and the sacrificial fanaticism of the Cult. They are beloved by the grunts they serve alongside, a symbol of the hope that the Mandate is fighting for something more than mere survival—they are fighting to preserve the very soul of humanity.

name: Marine
desc: The Mandate Marine is the inheritor of a legacy they can barely remember. Clad in worn, functional armor and wielding a rugged, reliable assault rifle, they are the grim face of the Terran Mandate's endless war to restore order. Each Marine is a professional soldier, drilled in the squad-based tactics that defined the old Federation's peacekeeping forces. They fight not for glory or faith, but for the fading memory of a better time—a time of peace and exploration their grandparents spoke of. They are the thin line holding back corporate greed, religious fanaticism, and the all-consuming Chorus. While they lack the advanced technology of the Syndicate or the zealous fury of the Cult, they possess a stubborn resolve forged in the ashes of a fallen utopia. They are the wall against which the darkness of the Interregnum breaks.

name: Corrupted ATV
desc: The Chorus does not build; it corrupts. This vehicle was once a Mandate "Warthog" ATV, a symbol of rugged reliability. Now, it is a mindless horror, a perversion of its former purpose. The original chassis is warped and twisted, its metal fused with pulsating organic growths and plates of glistening chitin. Sinewy tendrils have replaced wiring, and the engine's roar has been replaced by a wet, guttural chugging as it mindlessly charges into enemy lines. It is no longer a machine of reconnaissance but a living battering ram, a simple but effective tool of the hive mind's will. Each Corrupted ATV is a testament to the Chorus's insidious nature, a mobile monument to the fact that in the face of the swarm, nothing is sacred, and everything can be turned into a weapon.

name: Prospector
desc: In the vast, uncaring machinery of the Aurigan Trade Syndicate, the Prospector is the most common and expendable component. Lured from desperate colonies with promises of wealth, these individuals are given cheap environmental suits, rudimentary geological scanners, and a one-way contract to the most hostile worlds in the galaxy. They are the first boots on the ground in the relentless search for Aetherium, their lives measured in quotas and operational expenditures. They are not soldiers, but their casualty rates are higher than any frontline unit. Each Prospector knows that the strange readings on their scanner could lead to a life of unimaginable luxury or, more likely, a swift and anonymous death from atmospheric toxins, predatory fauna, or the very substance they seek. They are the human cost of every Syndicate war machine and every luxury enjoyed by the faceless Board of Directors.
